context.body: The Ziphites came to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “Doesn’t David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before the desert?”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: David and Abishai enter Saul’s camp, take spear and water jar, refuse to strike the anointed king, and call across the distance until Saul blesses David.
observations.label: Saul is spared in the camp: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Abishai, Saul, Abner, and the Ziphites, the hill of Hachilah and Saul’s sleeping camp, scouting, entering, refusing, taking tokens, calling, confessing, and separating visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Saul is spared in the camp: action, promise, or consequence

payload.posture: Read 1 Samuel 26:1–25 as its own flight, covenant, and restraint David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places restraint recurs with different objects, witnesses, and words inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
